clue.text: Beers smug drunk sinks

indicators.note: someone drunk staggers about in disorder, so the letters before it lose their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A self-satisfied drinker knocks back pints one after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' looks like a description of the smug drinker, but it only tells you to rearrange the nine letters of the first two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To submerge something is to push it under water, which is exactly what sinking it means as a verb.

clue.text: One in party with foremost of Soviet Trotskyites?

definitions.text: One in party with foremost of Soviet Trotskyites?

parts.note: a social is an informal party or gathering
the Roman numeral for one
the leading letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A question about a party member who sits with the leading Soviet followers of Trotsky.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a socialist could well be in a party alongside Trotskyites, hence the question mark. Note the pieces follow party, then one, then the two initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Trotskyites are a strand of the political left, so a party member among them is plausibly a socialist.

clue.text: Time to tuck into Indonesian island dish

indicators.note: to tuck into something is to go inside it, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: Bali is a well-known island of Indonesia
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: It is time to start eating some speciality food from Indonesia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tuck into' looks like the eating verb but it puts the T inside the island name. A balti is a curry cooked and served in a metal pan, popular in Birmingham, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A balti is a type of curry served in its cooking pot, so it is one specific example of a dish.

clue.text: Fancy a beer a lot, having gone off the rails

indicators.note: a train off its rails is wrecked and out of order, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who really wants a beer after losing control of their life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' reads as a verb meaning want, but the definition is the adjective meaning ornate or intricate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fancy is ornate and highly detailed, and elaborate is a synonym describing that intricate design.

clue.text: What plays a part in making one drop scones? Good and puzzling question!

definitions.text: What plays a part in making one drop scones?

parts.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
a riddle is a question designed to puzzle

explanation.surface: A baker's quiz: what helps you make drop scones?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop' seems to mean letting the scones fall. Drop scones are small thick pancakes, known in Scotland and England, cooked on a flat iron plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A griddle is the flat heavy cooking plate traditionally used to cook drop scones or Scotch pancakes.

clue.text: A part cut off German blokes during first of surgeries on film

indicators.note: first of asks for only the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: opening letter of the word

indicators.note: something happening during an event sits inside its span, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: E.T. is Spielberg's 1982 film about an alien
G is the abbreviation for German
blokes is British slang for men

explanation.surface: German men undergoing an amputation filmed during an operation.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the surgery initial sits on top of the film containing G and MEN; the surface pushes amputation, but 'cut off' just describes a separate portion.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment is a separate portion divided from a whole, like each piece of an orange.

clue.text: Singer right to break wind by saxophonist's head

indicators.note: to break into something is to force a way inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: gas is flatulence, or wind in the stomach
R is the abbreviation for right

indicators.note: a word's head is its top or front, so only the opening letter is wanted

parts.note: opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A singer next to the saxophonist's head is right to pass wind, a crude band-room joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' suggests a vocalist, but in British slang to sing is to inform to the police, and a grass is a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: In British criminal slang an informer sings to police, and grass is the common noun for that informer.

clue.text: Man starting on perilous journey in space after end of training!

indicators.note: end of asks for only the final letter of the following word

parts.note: closing letter of the word
room means space, as in room to move

explanation.surface: An astronaut sets off on a dangerous mission into space once his training ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The space voyage is the misdirection: the perilous journey is marriage, a tongue-in-cheek definition of a man on his wedding day.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridegroom is a man setting out on married life, jokingly painted here as a risky expedition.

clue.text: Good facts about natural disasters, perhaps

indicators.note: about can mean around in a muddle, so the preceding letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some sound information concerning earthquakes and floods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' reads as concerning but is the anagram signal. 'Perhaps' marks natural disasters as one example of the category.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurance and legal language calls events beyond human control acts of God, and earthquakes or floods are typical examples.

clue.text: Fire very old Tory leader that's injected heroin

indicators.note: an injection puts something inside a body, so one piece is put within the rest

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: the leader goes first, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: opening letter of the word
H is drug slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Sack an aged Conservative party leader who has been taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The first three pieces make SOOT, and the drug letter is put after its first letter. 'Fire' suggests dismissal but here means discharge a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire a gun is to shoot it, so the two verbs are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Fantastic carolling can be arresting

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful or bizarre, so the letters are reworked into something strange

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Wonderful Christmas singing can be striking and attention-grabbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arresting' looks like striking, praise for the singing, but it means taking into police custody.
explanation.definitionFit: Collar is informal slang for a police arrest, so collaring someone means arresting them.

clue.text: Beat United with balls going round the outside

indicators.note: pieces going round the outside surround the rest, so they enclose another piece

parts.note: balls are round, so each looks like the letter O
Utd is the usual abbreviation for United in football club names

explanation.surface: A football report: beating Manchester United with balls played round the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: Utd is how British football results abbreviate United, as in Man Utd.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat a rival is to do better than them, which is exactly what outdo means.

clue.text: Is Hoskins close to blotto after downing drop of gin and Bud in Spain?

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece coming after another simply follows it in order

parts.note: Hoskins is the setter, who would say 'am I' of himself

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its last letter is taken

parts.note: opening letter of the word

indicators.note: a drop is a tiny amount, so only a single opening letter is wanted

parts.note: closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: The setter wonders if he is nearly drunk after a gin and a Budweiser on a Spanish holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Bud reads as the American beer, but it is short for buddy. The setter's name stands for 'I', so 'Is Hoskins' turns into 'am I'.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is the Spanish word for friend, and bud is informal English for a close friend or buddy.

clue.text: Very hot man in boater mad to go out

indicators.note: to go out of shape is to lose form, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written; a boater is a flat straw hat

explanation.surface: A sweltering man in a straw hat, crazy enough to head outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the letters to be rearranged. 'Very hot' seems to mean sweltering, but means very attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamboat is an informal term for a strikingly attractive man, which is what calling him very hot implies.

clue.text: I make love outside Congress to reproduce, perhaps

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something outside another surrounds it, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: to mate is to have sex
it is a euphemism for sex, and congress is an old word for intercourse

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark about having sex in order to produce children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Congress' looks like the American legislature, but it is sexual intercourse, which crosswords often reduce to IT. 'Reproduce' suggests breeding but means copy.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate something is to copy it, and reproducing a picture or style is one way of copying it.

clue.text: Breathing in is stimulating to mind and spirit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: drawing air into the lungs, the literal sense of the verb

explanation.surface: A wellness tip: deep breathing is good for mind and spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb's original sense is literally to breathe in; the figurative sense of filling someone with ideas grew from it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both inhaling air, its literal Latin root sense, and rousing the mind and emotions, its figurative sense.

clue.text: This evening firm will restrict working!

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: tight means firmly fixed, as a firm knot
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A company announces that it will limit work later today.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company noun but is the adjective, and 'working' means switched on.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonight refers to the coming night of the present day, the same period as this evening.

clue.text: A pair of Republicans featuring in local story

indicators.note: something featuring in another appears inside it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: a native is a local person, born in the place
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for Republican, doubled for a pair

explanation.surface: Two Republican politicians appear in a hometown newspaper article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local story' reads as a news item, but 'local' is wordplay, a native of the place, and only 'story' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative is an account of connected events, which is what a story is.

clue.text: Streets PM wanders to find lady of a seductive bent

indicators.note: to wander is to stray from a set path, so the letters drift out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A prime minister walks the streets looking for a lady of the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PM' looks like the prime minister or afternoon but its two letters just join the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A temptress is a woman who sets out to seduce or entice men, someone with a seductive inclination.

clue.text: On Shrove Tuesday, cooks might be these sorts of idiots

definitions.text: On Shrove Tuesday, cooks might be these sorts of idiots

parts.note: surface reading: a British insult for contemptible fools
setter's reading: on Pancake Day cooks flip pancakes into the air

explanation.walkthrough: Shrove Tuesday is Pancake Day in Britain, when pancakes are flipped in the pan. The answer is also a vulgar British slang insult for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooks flipping pancakes are literally people who throw them up, while the same word is coarse British slang for idiots.

clue.text: Soprano as well as a queen with billions in offshore bank

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for soprano
and means as well as
B is the abbreviation for billions
taken as written
R stands for regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: An opera singer and a queen keep billions stashed in a tax-haven bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offshore bank' suggests a tax haven, but the bank is a ridge of sand in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandbar is a long ridge of sand built up in water near a coast, a bank lying offshore.

clue.text: Soldiers in base recalled Missouri as "state of no interest"

indicators.note: being in something means sitting within it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a bed is a base, as in a flower bed or seabed
OR stands for Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters run back the other way

parts.note: MO is the postal abbreviation for Missouri

explanation.surface: Troops at a military base look back on Missouri as a dull state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like one of the US states, a nice trick after Missouri, but it is a state of mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Boredom is the weary feeling of having nothing interesting to engage you, a condition with no interest.

clue.text: Food served up, then the French bread at last is broken into

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top, so letters run backwards

parts.note: grub is informal for food
le is French for the

indicators.note: at last points to the very end of the word, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: Food is served, then a French loaf is finally torn open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken into' seems to describe the bread being torn, but it means a house entered by thieves.
explanation.definitionFit: A building that has been burgled has been entered illegally by thieves, the sense of broken into.

clue.text: A fortifying drink is what might make Hoskins get up!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a strong alcoholic drink taken to steady the nerves

definitions.text: what might make Hoskins get up!
definitions.note: a cheeky description rather than a dictionary sense
definitions.meaning: second meaning: something that makes a thing rigid, with a saucy hint about the setter

explanation.surface: The setter jokes that a bracing drink is what gets him out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get up' looks like rising in the morning, but the setter is making a risque joke about arousal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff drink is a strong one, so a stiffener is a bracing alcoholic drink; the word also means anything that makes something rigid.

clue.text: Jerk from Sweden involved in unsolicited emails

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be wrapped up inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: spam is unwanted bulk email
S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

explanation.surface: A Swedish idiot is mixed up in sending junk mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' looks like an insult for a person, but here it is a sudden involuntary twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A spasm is a sudden involuntary muscle contraction, the kind of convulsive movement called a jerk.

clue.text: Liberal and earl taken in by brief diet could be suckers

indicators.note: something brief is cut short, so the word loses its final letter
to be taken in is to be received inside, so pieces go within another

parts.note: a fast is a diet of no food, cut short here
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
E is the abbreviation for earl

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician and an aristocrat fall for a crash diet, gullible fools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suckers' looks like dupes taken in by a diet, but it means bloodsuckers.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleas are tiny parasitic insects that feed on blood, so they are literally suckers.

clue.text: Actor in Bond?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who acts or brings something about

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks for a performer who played James Bond, but the actor is anyone who acts and Bond himself is the spy.
explanation.definitionFit: Agent originally means one who acts or performs a deed, and James Bond is the archetypal secret service spy.

clue.text: Furry little fellows found in Chinese wok, sizzling!

indicators.note: something found in a phrase is already sitting inside those words

parts.note: runs across the end of the first word, the whole second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Small furry animals turn up sizzling in a Chinese wok.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites a grim cooking image, but the letters run across three words and the furry fellows are from Star Wars.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewoks are the small, teddy-bear-like forest creatures in Star Wars: Return of the Jedi.

clue.text: Tolerate a president pinching bottom

indicators.note: pinching means stealing, so the lowest end of the name is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
Joe Biden, US president, with his last letter removed

explanation.surface: Putting up with a president who gropes people's backsides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinching' looks like groping, but it means stealing the name's bottom, its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide something is to put up with or endure it, as in 'I can't abide noise'.

clue.text: Two soldiers carrying medical officer in a US city

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it within, so pieces enclose another

parts.note: the answer to clue 2, the curry dish
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
MO is the abbreviation for medical officer

explanation.surface: A pair of troops carry an injured army doctor through an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two' looks like a number of soldiers but is a cross-reference to the answer at 2 down, the curry dish. The doctor sits between the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Baltimore is the largest city in Maryland, a major port on the East Coast of the United States.

clue.text: Dodging Nakamura's opening, Carlsen is a wise man

indicators.note: dodging means avoiding, so that letter is left out of the name

parts.note: Magnus Carlsen, the Norwegian chess world champion

indicators.note: an opening is the very start, so only the first letter is meant

parts.note: opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: Chess commentary: Carlsen sidesteps Nakamura's opening move and proves a genius.
explanation.walkthrough: Hikaru Nakamura and Magnus Carlsen are top chess grandmasters, so 'opening' sounds like a chess term but just takes the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A magus is a learned sage or sorcerer, like the Magi, the three wise men of the Nativity.

clue.text: Puts right ginger locks without any tinting essentially

parts.note: ginger hair is red

indicators.note: without any means lacking, so that letter is removed entirely

parts.note: tresses are long locks of hair

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only the central letter is wanted

parts.note: the middle letter of the word, which is then deleted

explanation.surface: Fixing someone's red hair without using any dye at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essentially' takes the heart of the colouring word, and that letter is then dropped from the front of the hair word.
explanation.definitionFit: To redress a wrong or an imbalance is to correct it, so the verb means puts right.
